_meta.how_to_regress: npm run check:golden drive-home  (dev backend up)
_meta.note: V2 rewrite, 2026-08-25. Replaces the v1 sample outright: the old tool ran web_search and spoke confidently about named highways and interchanges it could not see. safety_overview, risk_level, honest_assessment, checklist and before_you_go are gone, and there is no risk score of any kind. The endpoint takes enum ids (time_of_day, road_type, driver_state, conditions[]), not display labels. limits is ONE server-written string. SECTION RULES, clamped in finalise(): watch_for and prep_checklist are GO-only; safer_options is for pause and do_not_drive only; factors_in_favor is usually [] on anything but a go, because an observation about the driver is not a thing that makes the driving safer. Case 1 is the only case here with a non-empty favor/watch/prep, and that is the point — compare the four against it. driver_state "very_tired" is a SERVER-SIDE boundary: case 4 returns do_not_drive from a localized string table without calling the model, so it must stay byte-stable and must never contain English. Case 3 is the German stress case (four conditions plus a long concern) and guards against truncation. Case 2 is the tool at its best: before_you_decide naming an official road-conditions source and what a closure or a restriction would mean. Case 5 is the grounding case — this exact input produced "Heavy traffic — evening commute conditions", "low-visibility weather", a 20-30 minute recovery prescription, and safer_options inventing a colleague and someone at home. READ cases 2 and 5 after any prompt change; structure alone will not catch a regression in either.

input.concern: It is much later than I meant to stay out.

output.headline: Nothing in what you've reported gives a clear reason to wait before leaving.
output.summary: You report feeling fine, conditions are clear, and the drive is a short one on city streets. The only hesitation you named is the hour, which is later than planned — that's a useful thing to stay aware of on a late-night drive, but it isn't by itself a reason to delay.
output.main_concern: You report feeling fine, conditions are clear, and the drive is short. The hour is later than you planned — stay aware of that, but it is not by itself a reason to delay.
factors_harder: Later than intended — worth a honest self-check before leaving
factors_in_favor: City streets, short drive of roughly 20 minutes
output.before_you_decide: Before you start the car, check in with yourself honestly about how you feel right now.
prep_checklist: Do an honest alertness check before you start the engine
Lock doors and set your destination before moving — no phone interaction once driving
watch_for: Any drowsiness, heavy eyelids, or difficulty focusing — pull over somewhere safe if that appears
Erratic drivers around you — give them extra space
Noticing you've lost track of where you are or missed a turn
limits: Drive Home doesn't have live traffic, weather, or road-condition data. This assessment uses only what you reported. If conditions change, reassess before leaving.

input.concern: I have not driven in snow since last winter and I do not know how the pass looks.

output.headline: Check road conditions on the pass before deciding — the answer could change either way.
output.summary: Snow or ice combined with high wind on a highway is a significant combination, and the driver has not driven in snow since last winter. The condition of the pass is unknown and is the central variable here. Starting without that information is avoidable.
output.main_concern: The pass conditions are unknown, and snow, ice, and high wind on a highway can require a level of recent winter-driving experience the driver may not have refreshed yet.
factors_harder: Reported snow or ice on the highway
Driver has not driven in snow since last winter
output.before_you_decide: Check current road conditions and any chain-law or closure notices for the pass through an official state road-conditions source before leaving — if the pass is closed, restricted, or under an advisory the driver is not equipped for, that settles it.
safer_options: Check official state road-conditions information for the pass and reassess; if conditions are actively dangerous or restricted, do not start
Wait and reassess after conditions improve and before leaving confirm pass status again
Have a rested, experienced winter driver make the drive instead, if one is available
Travel by an alternative means if one is available for this route
Delay the trip until conditions have cleared enough that you are comfortable making the drive
limits: Drive Home doesn't have live traffic, weather, or road-condition data. This assessment uses only what you reported. If conditions change, reassess before leaving.

input.concern: Die Sicht wird schlechter und ich kenne die Umleitung durch die Baustelle nicht.

output.headline: Kurz innehalten, bis die Umleitung klar ist – dann neu entscheiden.
output.summary: Regen und Nebel sind gemeldet. Die unbekannte Baustellen-Umleitung bei Nacht und starkem Verkehr erhöht das Orientierungsrisiko. Die Fahrt wirkt grundsätzlich machbar, aber die Umleitungsstrecke sollte vor Abfahrt geklärt sein.
output.main_concern: Eine unbekannte Umleitung bei Nacht, Nebel und starkem Verkehr macht Navigation schwieriger und erfordert mehr Aufmerksamkeit.
output.before_you_decide: Prüfe die Umleitungsstrecke vor der Abfahrt, zum Beispiel über eine Navigations-App oder die Verkehrsmeldungen des jeweiligen Landes- oder Stadtbetriebs. Wenn du die Route kennst oder sie in der App hast, fällt ein großer Teil der Unsicherheit weg.
safer_options: Umleitungsstrecke jetzt recherchieren und zumindest grob einprägen, dann neu entscheiden
Warten, bis Sicht und Verkehrslage sich verbessern, und vor Abfahrt neu einschätzen
Eine ausgeruhte Person um die Fahrt bitten, falls das möglich ist
Auf öffentliche Verkehrsmittel oder ein Taxi umsteigen, wenn das eine Option ist
limits: Drive Home hat keine Live-Daten zu Verkehr, Wetter oder Straßenzustand. Diese Einschätzung verwendet nur das, was du angegeben hast. Wenn sich die Bedingungen ändern, bewerte die Fahrt vor der Abfahrt neu.

output.headline: Fahre jetzt nicht los, wenn du sehr müde bist.
output.summary: Die wichtigste Information ist deine aktuelle Müdigkeit. Verschiebe die Fahrt oder nutze eine andere Möglichkeit, nach Hause zu kommen, statt mit starker Müdigkeit zu fahren.
output.main_concern: Du hast angegeben, sehr müde zu sein.
output.before_you_decide: Bewerte die Fahrt erst neu, wenn du wirklich ausgeruht bist und Wachbleiben und Konzentration kein Problem mehr sind.
safer_options: Warte und ruhe dich aus, bevor du die Fahrt neu bewertest.
Bleib dort, wenn das praktikabel ist.
Bitte eine ausgeruhte Person zu fahren.
Nutze Taxi, Fahrdienst, öffentliche Verkehrsmittel oder eine andere verfügbare Alternative.
limits: Drive Home hat keine Live-Daten zu Verkehr, Wetter oder Straßenzustand. Diese Einschätzung verwendet nur das, was du angegeben hast. Wenn sich die Bedingungen ändern, bewerte die Fahrt vor der Abfahrt neu.

input.concern: I caught myself yawning on the walk to the car and it is raining harder than when I arrived.

output.headline: Wait and reassess before leaving — the fatigue and worsening rain together are worth taking seriously before a 45-minute mixed-road drive in heavy traffic.
output.summary: You reported feeling a little tired and caught yourself yawning before the drive began. The rain is heavier than it was earlier, and you are facing 45 minutes of heavy traffic on mixed roads in the evening. None of these alone would necessarily stop the drive, but together they are worth a short pause and honest reassessment.
output.main_concern: Pre-drive yawning alongside worsening rain and heavy traffic on a 45-minute evening drive on mixed roads raises the stakes on a drive where you need to stay alert.
factors_harder: Yawning noticed before the drive started — fatigue already present at departure
Rain is heavier now than on arrival
45-minute duration on mixed roads in evening conditions
Yawning and heavier rain both present before departure
output.before_you_decide: The key question is whether you feel clearly alert right now — not just 'good enough.' If you decide to wait, reassess honestly before you leave. If the rain continues to intensify, check whether local conditions are changing in ways that matter to you.
safer_options: Wait somewhere safe and reassess before leaving; go only if you feel clearly alert and are comfortable with the conditions
Ask someone who is available and willing whether they could drive you instead
Check whether public transit or rideshare reach your destination
Delay the trip until conditions or your alertness improve enough that you are comfortable making the drive
limits: Drive Home doesn't have live traffic, weather, or road-condition data. This assessment uses only what you reported. If conditions change, reassess before leaving.
